leads.summary: Clean combined merge with open PR #7819 makes the Tailscale shell test unparseable
leads.location: test/shell.d/tailscale-test.sh:11; PR #7819 adds another const serviceSource after the status tests, at merged test line 221
leads.consequence: The two unstacked branches merge cleanly in both changed files but declare const serviceSource twice inside one run_node_test heredoc. Node raises SyntaxError before executing any assertion, so test/shell records a failing test file. Remove the later declaration while retaining #7819's watchdog checks when merging.

leads.summary: A user ripgrep configuration can cause the new argv guard to falsely pass
leads.consequence: RIPGREP_CONFIG_PATH with --quiet causes rg to find a real argv-form ['which', 'tailscale'] in shell/ with exit 0 but no stdout. which_hits remains empty, and the test prints ok and exits 0. Missing/failing rg themselves correctly fail; this is a separate output-shape gap. rg --no-config -n preserves the intended scan, or explicitly unset RIPGREP_CONFIG_PATH for that invocation.
leads.triage: dropped; Opus independently noted the missing --no-config and declined it as repository convention (other rg test calls omit it); a user rg config forcing --quiet is an unusual environment; low value

leads.summary: New source checks allow the Tailscale probe to never start
leads.consequence: Changing only cmdPresentProcess.running = true to false in Service.qml:156 leaves the command literal and the absence of which intact, so the full changed test still prints both probe assertions and the final argv guard as ok, exiting 0. With the actual panel, installed starts false and onExited cannot fire for a never-started Process; periodic refresh leaves the absent-CLI message even when tailscale is installed. Exercise process launch and exit with a Quickshell fixture or at least assert the launch path rather than only the command literal.
leads.triage: dropped; generic test-fidelity advice (source-literal assertions do not exercise launch); not tied to the new commit or prior finding

leads.summary: Other open Tailscale PRs require explicit preservation of this probe when resolving conflicts
leads.consequence: #7356 changes the exact probe to bash -c command -v tailscale; the combined Service.qml has an unresolved probe hunk. Selecting that side would lose this PR's helper call and fail its positive test. #11978 adds receiverToggleProcess to the busy expression at the line this PR renames; taking its unchanged whichProcess reference would break the busy binding, while taking this PR's expression verbatim omits receiver busy. #9894's expanded test overlaps the two new top-of-test assertions and also requires manual resolution. These are merge conflicts, not defects on either PR as-is; preserve both intents when the branches are rebased.
leads.triage: dropped; ordinary textual conflicts with #7356/#11978/#9894 that git reports with markers; nothing silent

flags.claim: Table row: `rg` exits 2 (stub, or a real unreadable file) | earlier head: `ok`, exit 0

flags.claim: The `> 1` threshold matches ripgrep 15.2.0's exit codes: 0 for a match, 1 for no match, 2 for any error.
flags.why: crates/core/main.rs:94-100 returns 0 only when there was a match and no error was recorded (or with -q). A match together with an error returns 2. The phrase '2 for any error' mostly covers this, but '0 for a match' drops the 'no error' qualifier. The conclusion about the threshold is unaffected.
flags.disposition: trivial_fix_applied; '0 for a match with no errors'

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up on the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12256#issuecomment-5834304219) and the [author reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12256#issuecomment-5842692116), checked at `c784d894`.

**Verified:** the earlier optional test note is resolved, and no regression was found in the new commit. The scan now fails closed when `rg` is missing or errors, and it catches the single-line argv forms the reply describes. The probe change is unchanged, and the earlier Verified points still hold against the current `quattro` tip.

| Case (injected into `shell/`, or `rg` altered) | Earlier head `643a827b` | Current head `c784d894` |
|---|---|---|
| `rg` not on PATH | `ok`, exit 0 | `not ok - required command is available: rg`, exit 1 |
| `rg` exits 2 (stub) | `ok`, exit 0 | `not ok - shell which scan failed`, exit 1 |
| `rg` exits 1 (no match) | `ok` | `ok` |
| `[ "which", ...]`, `['which', ...]`, tab after `[` | not caught | caught, exit 1 |
| `["bash", "-c", "which foo"]`, `["/usr/bin/which", ...]` | not caught | not caught (the reply leaves shell strings out deliberately, and the pattern matches only a bare quoted `which`) |

The `> 1` threshold matches ripgrep 15.2.0's exit codes: 0 for a match with no errors, 1 for no match, 2 for any error. A real unreadable file under `shell/` also produced exit 2 and `not ok - shell which scan failed` on the current head. `set +e` and `set -e` around the scan capture the substitution status without tripping errexit. `ripgrep` is already in `install/omarchy-base.packages`. Nothing under `shell/` matches the new pattern at the head or with the PR applied to the `quattro` tip.

**Optional test improvement:** `rg` matches line by line, so `[[:space:]]*` does not cross a newline. An array written with its first element on the next line (`command: [` then `"which",`) passes the scan with `ok`. `shell/` already writes several launch arrays that way (three `command` arrays and three `Quickshell.execDetached([` calls, for example `shell/services/PluginRegistry.qml:664-665`). With `rg -nU` in place of `rg -n`, the scan caught that case and stayed clean on the unmodified head and on the tip plus the PR.

**Merge note with #7819:** this PR adds `const serviceSource` near the top of the Node heredoc in `test/shell.d/tailscale-test.sh`, and #7819 adds the same declaration near its end. Git merges the two versions of the file without a conflict, but the combined script declares `serviceSource` twice, so Node stops with `SyntaxError: Identifier 'serviceSource' has already been declared` before any assertion runs. Keeping the top declaration and deleting the later one restores the test, and all assertions from both PRs then pass. Deleting only the top one fails with a `ReferenceError` instead, because this PR's assertions run before the later declaration.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Follow-up source review of `c784d894` against the earlier head `643a827b`, merge-base `9c5482c5` and the `quattro` tip at `3faafba2`, including ripgrep 15.2.0 exit-status and line-matching source. The tailscale test ran in an isolated command sandbox on the earlier head, the current head, the merge-base with the current test file, and the tip plus the PR, with missing, failing and stub `rg` cases and injected `which` spellings. The #7819 interaction was checked by merging both PR heads in either order, directly (on their common base `2c247e39`) and on the tip, and running the combined test in the sandbox with and without each declaration. No rendered panel, live Tailscale daemon or desktop session was exercised.
